candidates.function: Find ripe food of kinds your own eating records support in an area; gather one unit, then eat it; one navigate, probe, gather or eat step per round within limits.
bounded-resource-search-recheck plus lowHealth: a bounded search while health is low that stops at a health threshold you set (20 or more) instead of 60.
bounded-resource-search plus options: recheck sources last seen empty, an emergency mode for low satiety, stricter health and temperature stops, avoided areas or directions.

execution.progress: start or resume continues with the same action, one step per round, until it completes or stops; a round taken by another action pauses it. Steps and costs stay.

details.costs: None of its own: each round is one ordinary step at its own cost. navigate: distance x 2 energy, raised by ground and load, at most 0.8 per round; probe observe: 1 round, 0.2 energy; gather: 1 round, 2 energy per unit. Each step is priced first against the path, time and energy left and the reserve; one that does not fit is not taken. time counts every round since start, paused ones too. Study: 1 round; needs navigate, probe and gather.
details.effects: Without lowHealth: exactly bounded-resource-search-recheck (minHealth 60 to 100). lowHealth: true: health at or below minHealth (default 20, 20 to 100) stops it instead of health 60, and satiety <= 8 or starvation damage alone does not; any other injury in the last round, body temperature 12 or below or 32 or above, minTemp, maxTemp, the reserve and every limit still do. radius, path, time, energy and quantity must be above 0. A food search needs reserve >= 1 and your own eating record of that food as edible and nontoxic. Ripe sources seen now or remembered in the radius first, nearest first; with recheck, then sources last seen empty, each probed at most once per run; a remembered place is only a navigate destination. Another action pauses it; resume rechecks; cancel or death ends it. Nothing is refunded, created, eaten or healed; no reward; food is not assured.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

retrieval.access: Search/index only; omission is not absence. Use exact ids and zero-based offset/part for full records. No physical observation, state change or reward is performed.

value.name: Assess food suitability
value.function: Judge whether an item or source within reach is suitable food for you or a person you see, from probe evidence and your own cited records: identity, nutrition, toxicity and preparation each supported, contradicted or unresolved. inspect observes it with probe; trial runs probe press, wet or heat on your own sample. Nothing is tasted, eaten or fed.
value.costs: Study 1 round, no energy; needs probe. inspect: probe observe, 1 round, 0.2 energy, no material. trial (methodRef press, wet or heat; intensity is the press load): probe's trial, 1 round, 0.5 energy and 0.1 unit of your own sample, consumed as loss; heat also takes 0.1 available heat from a source in reach, wet needs water where you stand. A trial needs a cited verified probe record of the same kind, method and load to compare with, since a load, water or heat response measures no nutrition, harm or preparation; otherwise it is refused, naming what is missing. Refusals cost nothing: target not seen now (only remembered or named), out of reach, another person's item, not a material, consumer not you or a person you see, unknown record ids. No surcharge, no refund.
value.effects: target: exact id of your item, a loose item or a source in reach. evidenceRefs: up to 6 ids of your records (record key or its evidence id, an eating record by its kind, a heard message id). intendedConsumer: you by default or a person you see; only your own records are used. Identity is supported only by your own eating record of the same kind, never by a name or label; only then are its satiety and health loss cited, and preparation is none for units as you ate them. A trial response that differs from the reference contradicts identity; a match identifies nothing. Without applicable evidence: "safety unresolved; do not consume on this evidence." An event and your record <target>:food-suitability keep the findings, evidence and limits. Nothing is gathered, moved, created, detoxified, certified or rewarded.

execution.progress: Atomic: each mode completes in its one round and commits with its event; a refused or interrupted round commits nothing, and a retry is a new paid round. Nothing is reserved or left pending.
